newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Thursday due to falls on the domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract fell to 6.70 percent from 7.99 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market soared to 7.4 million lots from 3.5 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Share prices on both the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges fell on Thursday, reducing demand for funds on the repo market, traders said.
"The repo rates opened high and closed down just like the Shanghai A share market," one trader said.
But a new A share issue on the Shenzhen stock exchange supported the early-maturing contracts, traders said.
The contracts are likely to move around the current level on Friday with no fresh market-moving news in sight, they said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Thursday on a technical correction with market sentiment remaining good, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond maturing in June 2006 rose to 118.95 yuan from 118.79. The other six contracts ended down.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 1.6 million lots from 2.1 million lots.
Traders said sentiment was strong due to improvements in market fundamentals including ample money supply as a result of the recent heavy redemption of state debts.
They said they believed the spot contracts would recover soon.
